name: notifypermit
algorithm: two workers (Mk: tasks; Go: goroutines; Rust and Zig: OS threads) alternate n times, each waking the other, each language with its std's permit-style primitive (SYNC2-R3): Mk one sync.Notify per side (NotifyOne stores a permit, Wait consumes it); Rust std::thread::park and Thread::unpark over a flag per side (park's documented pattern); Go one chan struct{} of capacity 1 per side (non-blocking send, receive); Zig one std.Io.Event per side (set; wait, then reset). No lock and no turn variable on any side. Each counts its rounds; prints the total (README.md).

skip.c: no permit-style primitive in standard C (C11 <threads.h> has mtx_t and cnd_t only, which the notify row compares; sem_t is POSIX)
skip.mk-wrap: the only arithmetic is the round counters, which stay below 2^40

no_counts: B24 does not apply: the total, 2 * n, shows every round completed on both sides
notes: Concurrency row (B19): every column runs on logical CPUs 0 and 2 (mask 0x5, two physical cores) with 2 threads (MK_CARRIERS=2, GOMAXPROCS=2), as the notify and chan rows.

Written by std-sync2 for review finding SYNC2-R3 (status/std-sync2.md, M6 fix round). The notify row sets Mk's Notify beside condition variables (a mutex, a turn and a condition per side): the comparison D-375 makes, but not like with like. This row is the like-for-like one. The Mk program is the notify row's.
